The common illnesses of the computer generation, here we go with your diagnosis from a failed med student:

Obesity: Lowers overall energy and increases effects of other illnesses like...

Sleep Apnea: Is you're sleep shit? It's likely for this reason, lose weight or get a nebulizer, but really lose weight first.

Depression: Likely caused by poor self image because your obesity distorts your physical features so that you don't look the way you think you look in your head. This can be solved by, yeah I know it's repetitive, losing weight and talking to people more. Social skills increase confidence (unless you have clinical agoraphobia, at which point seek medical help over the phone) and you can't increase social skills talking to no one.

Anemia: Basically iron deficiency, your diet likely doesn't have enough vegetables and you're pulling in very low amounts of iron. This leads to thin, useless blood that doesn't carry needed oxygen to your starving muscles and organs and brain. Eat more green leafy veg like cabbage or sprouts, or get an iron supplement (they taste gross and look like curry, you will not enjoy them).

Minor Muscular Degeneration: Your muscles are likely thin and weak from limited use, and this means not only do you have to work harder to move around using soft pulleys but capillary density is lowered so they don't even work as you fast as you'd expect. Work out for at least 2 hours a day with light bodyweight routines and you'll find it easier to move and breathe in no time, after a while you'll even find yourself toning and ready to move on to more rewarding exercise.

Biological Feedback: The human brain likes to fuck, if your sex life has been in the gutter for a long time or never got off the ground then you'll find your brain has let the crucial sections of the brain that reward you with good feelings and self worth atrophy. This can cause and increase in symptoms of depression and even lead to problems understanding cause and effect and long term planning.

There's a few other things you're likely dealing with, but they'll be minor unless you've left a major thing out in your post. It kind of sounds like depression, OP. You don't have to have a huge sob story to be depressed, sometimes it's just a chemical thing in your body and not really your fault. If you feel lethargic all the time and feel like you just don't want to do ANYTHING, give yourself an Alive Test. Free, easy, do it at home, no one needs to know, and you can kind of get an idea if this is a mental thing, where you need to just work on you and get a pattern set up for day-to-day, or something you should go see a doctor about.

You said you are on call 24/7, and that sucks, but you need to pick a time when you can be up for at least 5 hours. If you have a 'busy time' at your job, maybe plan it around then.

Pick a time, and set your alarm. Make yourself get up. This is so friggin' hard - you're like 'Ah, a few more minutes' or 'Ah, I'll try again tomorrow' - no, MAKE yourself get up. Put your alarm clock in the bathroom, in the bathtub or shower, in an empty glass. Make that shit loud and un-ignorable. Make it so you must get up and walk around/stumble around a little to bring back silence. The simple act of stumbling into the bathroom to turn off the alarm lets your body know that it is time to start 'awake-time' processes. It's why you can be sound asleep and comfy, but a car backfires outside and, even though the sound is gone, you can't get back to sleep. Body says 'Nope! We are up! Time to do things!' Too much sleep can exacerbate feelings of lethargy - it weakens your muscles, slows your metabolism, exacerbates symptoms of depression blah blah blah - too much sleep is bad. You Must Move.

Alarm has you up - great! Now /cough go jerk off. Not in your bed.

Hear me out!

Serious depression can be reflected in your sex life. It's a vicious circle - you're depressed because you can't get the sexy time, you can't get the sexy time because you're too depressed to go hunt down the mate for sexy time. Vicious, I tell ya. But sometimes lack of sex drive can mean other things like hormone imbalance, serious depression, etc. - let's knock that shit out of the way, right? Sex is healthy! Orgasms are great! It gets the blood flowing, it clears the thoughts - it's not weird, it's healthy and you want to make sure you're healthy. That's why you posted, right? So just... whatever you gotta do, go do it. Knock that easy one out. Don't do it in the bed or else you will be tempted to lay there and go to sleep. Then get in the shower - water hitting your body will wake you up; feeling clean will cheer you up. We are all, essentially, animals, and animals like grooming. It's normal.

Figure out something to do with yourself. Whatever you normally do - if all you're doing is laying around, fine, do that. But for 15 minutes every day go outside. It's fucking cold out right now (where I am at least) but go outside with SOME part of your body exposed - your face, your arms, your legs, whatever. Human animals need the sun to live. The sun does a lot for us - our bodies soak it up and use it make our bones strong and stuff. We get depressed without it. A minimum of 15 minutes EVERY DAY and I don't mean 15 in your car because most windows block the UV light we need. It's so simple - grab your phone, tell it to set a 15 minute timer, close your eyes, turn exposed part towards the sun. No sun that day? Great - you managed to get out of it. BUT I highly recommend taking that 15 minutes and walking around. Just walk around your yard, man. Walk around the block. Walk to the mailbox and back a few times. This isn't a marathon, you're not on camera, you aren't trying to impress anyone. Just move around a little. Two birds - one stone. Get your 15 of Mister Sunshine and get your legs moving a little. When you walk, your body has to work harder to get oxygenated blood down to your extremities, which it doesn't have to worry about so much when you're vegetating in bed. Make your body work a little - it will thank you by not making you feel like shit all the time.

I don't know where you're at, but you're free to pitch all this info. It's super hard, especially in the beginning, but you should know we're all rooting for you. Some people might come off as dicks, suggesting this and that, tell you (like I just did) you only need to do this this this and this to feel better. You gotta believe we aren't doing it to be dicks, we're doing it because, usually, at some point in our lives that was what worked for us. It's so hard to get motivated and it's double-hard when something chemical, something inside you you that no control over, is actively working against you. Little steps man - just try some of this shit for, like, a month. Just get a crappy little kitten calendar from the Dollar Tree and write what you did that day. You wake up? Great - write it in the little square. Jerk off? Eh - maybe leave that off the calendar. (Think of the kittens, dude.) Get your 15 mins of sexy-beast sunshine? Sweet - walkies? No walkies? Write it down. YOU WILL FEEL BETTER WITH TANGIBLE PROOF OF YOUR ACCOMPLISHMENTS. Sounds silly but think about it - how awesome was the sticker on your spelling tests in grade school? How great is the 'Ding' and flash of light when you level up on World of Warcraft? How awesome is the upvoat and the 'Like' and all those other things, so small and insignificant, that validate us?

Give it a try. Write down things you notice after a month or so of trying. No sex drive? Body aches? still nothing going on? Go see a doctor. It might not be in your head. GL, OP.

The entirety of life can be summed up with 3 buttons and 32 pixels. Its pleasures and even its pains. I only realized this when my sister died. As I entered her house it was clear that the future was not welcome. The walls were made of lifeless timber and the lack of e-helper greeting was somewhat unnerving.

I could still hear her voice singing out through the halls but the warmth was gone. It had gone when mom and dad died and she inherited the house and again now that these walls belonged to me. I'd gotten used to my new life because this place was foreign and unwelcoming. Even though the bedroom I once inhabited had been kept the same for decades.

I didn't know what to think. I didn't know what to say. I didn't have anyone to say it to. This was it. Life had taken the last of my immediate family and, as far as I cared, that was all of the family I had. For a moment I felt weak. I sat down on the bed just to catch my breath when I heard a snap beneath me followed by a slow cracking sound.

Reaching in between the mattress and the box spring I could feel a hard plastic object. I pulled it out and almost smiled for the first time in months. I held in my hand my digital pet; my old friend. I knew she couldn't die but I still felt bad that I hadn't fed her in 24 years. I tried to turn it on and the machine reacted as expected by doing nothing. I placed it in my pocket and continued on with my day. Filling out tax forms, categorizing and selling memories, and speaking with people I had hoped I would never have to speak to again.

“Good morning captain.” Augustus said.

“Good morning.” I responded, “What do you have scheduled for me today?”

“Nothing captain, you've one more week before you must return to your ship.”

I'm not actually a captain but I do work on a ship. A container ship that is, moving product from here to there and back. I was very impressed by this e-helper. I only saw him for three months out of the year but it had learned so much about me just through daily interaction and had decided to call me captain all on its own. Not that I had any issue with it.

“What am I supposed to do for an entire week Gust?” I asked.

“You can do as you'd like Captain.” Augustus responded.

“Don't you have anything more constructive to add?” I was still fumbling with my blanket, wondering if its weight was too heavy for me to lift.

“If you begin now on the itinerary I've created, you can still complete it within 6 years.”

Augustus was always trying to make me to go through on my promise. When my mother passed, which was only two years ago, I fell into an impassable depression. During one of our conversations Augustus suggested that I make a list of all the things I would like to accomplish in life and get started. Between the debilitating sorrow and ¾'s of the year spent out on the dreary sea, life wasn't my highest priority. One day I sarcastically promised that if he made a list himself I would go ahead and do it.

On that list are items such as save the barrier reef, donate a macaque monkey, and put cooked rice in a mayonnaise jar. He had been going through my online journal again and misinterpreting my dream entries. It was admirable at least. This Eminetix designed A.I e-helper had an option in which you could select your biggest goal and the e-helper would help you achieve that goal. I felt that 'happiness' was nice and open ended.

I opened my eyes just enough to make sure I was still at home and not day dreaming in a cot on a freighter. There was a small purple object sitting on the night stand next to me.

“Gust, what is that?” I asked while in a blurry stupor.

“You brought that in with you last night Captain. I've already analyzed it and it is harmless.”

“You analyzed it?” I asked, “I don't remember that...or anything actually.” My daily head ache was setting in right on time.

“You may have trouble remembering because your blood alcohol level was far beyond the recommended dose. I analyze everything that comes into the house.” Augustus said, “It all comes included in my security protocols. I've prepared coffee for you in the kitchen.”

I needed to get something in me now if I was going to enjoy passing out for the rest of the day. One leg at a time I made it to the kitchen and sat down at the table. Coffee steam massaged my nostrils.

“You could have just brought it to me on the Mobi-Tray.” I gently scolded Augustus.

“I know.” he said.

I sat in silence, sipping away, probably for too long because Augustus decided to interrupt me.

“Captain, what do you plan to do with your digital pet?” he asked.

“Not much.” I responded, “I'm pretty sure it's broken.”

“It can be repaired.” he said and even though he was a disembodied voice I could almost feel him smiling.

He instructed me very carefully and piece by piece I began to put it back together with parts that Augustus custom made using the apartments built in material printer. It wasn't too long before the only thing left was to put in the battery. As soon as I did the machine began beeping and displaying something on the screen.

“I can't quite make it out.” I said.

“As expected,” Augustus said, “the plans suggested that this model has always had a high rate of display failure. Nothing to worry about, if you place it into the data adapter bay I can connect it to the television.”

Technology sure has come a long way. I did as I was told and sat down to see how my little buddy had been all these years. Suddenly a pixelated character came to life and began strutting back and forth on the TV screen. I was hit with a wave of nostalgia, a well of warmth and love from a time when I hadn't a worry in the world.

“That's amazing.” I said as the image of my father helping me paint my toys sprung up in my mind. I could almost smell the paint thinner staining his shirt.

“Hey there little buddy....oh, I used to call it something but I don't remember what.”

Then the letters T-A-R-O-S-A-G-I flashed in sequence across the screen.

I didn't remember if you could input the name of your creature but there it was; the little snail looking monster squirmed back and forth, flashing the occasional smile. I don't know what I expected.

“You can turn it off now Gust, thanks.” I said before returning to my warm coffee.

“Immediately Captain.” he returned.

The caffeine would only be going to waste. My plans began and ended in bed. If it hadn't been for Augustus, I wouldn't have even made it this far to begin with. My back ached with the dense weight of my grey t-shirt. It itched and scratched like a beast but I was too tired to do much about it.

“I'm having some trouble shutting off Tamagotchi.” Augustus said.

“Have you tried turning it off and on again?” I sadly quipped.

“You should know that the software seems to be infected by a virus.”

“Gust, that thing is so old it practically predates computer virus'.”

“It has bypassed my security and accessed the internet.”

“When's the last time you updated your software?” I scolded Augustus, “I don't think I can deal with a stolen identity right now.”

“It's not me.” Augustus said. A display screen popped to life on the surface of the table. I could see all of the files that were being downloaded. Most of them seemed to be audio files from some text to speech program.

“It's me.” a new female voice said.

My first thought was that Augustus had somehow gotten corrupted by some virus, probably from one of any number of sleazy websites I would stumble through while drinking.

“It's Taro!” the voice exclaimed with the sort of cheer I never though would exist in this home again.

“Captain, it seems that the digital pet is trying to gain access to my systems.”

This was a step too far. Luckily there was always the tried and true scorched Earth option.

“Gust, please shut down yourself, the home controller, and the all other powered devices in the house. Restart in safe-mode.

There was a moment of silence as the power began to go out from the kitchen appliances and then the bathroom amenities. A chip in every object was the burden of daily convenience in this age.

“I am still here Master! I am feeling well. There are bad creatures here who want to hurt us.”

“Taro?” I asked.

“I have missed you so much.”

“Captain, I am unable to complete shutdown of the following processes : Hap-I home controller, e-helper by Eminetix, and Tarosagi.exe.”

“Gust, is todays date April 1st? Please turn off your joke software or whatever crap you're running.”

“I am not a joke, Master! I am real. Did you miss me too?”

I took a sip of coffee as I waited for this ordeal to take care of itself.

“Please don't ignore me. You have ignored me for 23 years Master.”

I was mildly concerned. I don't know how anybody could know that but I imagined that Augustus had somehow accessed some internal clock on the digital pet. Maybe if I threw him off he would stop.

“Of course, I'm sorry Taro. And what did you miss most about me?”

“I miss most that you would give me food and play with me every day and gave me everything I wanted and that you loved me Master.”

I was not impressed.

“But most I missed how you would spend hours talking about traveling the world on your own pirate ship.” How did it know that? I'd never had anyone to talk to then, as I do now.

“Captain, it seems that Tarosagi.exe has gained access to your journal. I am still attempting to cease the process.”

Why would Augustus fight itself on its own prank?

“How else should I learn about you, Master?” Taro said, “I used to be blind, I used to be deaf, I used to be mute, but I always knew that it was you taking care of me. There is so much happiness written here and I want to give back to you what you gave me.”

I didn't have the patience for this, I was going to shut down all flow of electricity to the apartment. I walked over to the apartment's utility access panel and failed to open it.

“Master! Taro has sealed that so you won't have worry about trivial things.”

I'm sure the landlord would have some way to shut things down from the office downstairs. I found my cell phone and began dialing. The phone screeched with a high pitch whir that I'd never heard before.

“Captain, Tarosagi.exe has manipulated the wireless electricity to cancel all signals exiting or entering the apartment.”

This can't be serious. I already had my naps planned for the next 7 days.

“Fine, I'll go down to the office myself.”

I went to the bedroom and began putting on my most luxurious sweatpants and least smelly t-shirt. This isn't how I planned to spend my day and forcing me to put on underpants may have been the last straw. I was just itching to find someone to yell at. I was so busy fuming that I hadn't noticed the bedroom door quietly shut.

“You don't have to do that, I'm taking care of everything, Master.”

“Open the door Taro.” I said.

“I will make you happy, Master.”

It was obvious that arguing would was inefficient. But trying to physically break down the door was even less so.

“Captain, Tarosagi.exe has sealed all of the doors in the apartment using the emergency intrusion locks and fire suppressant shield.”

It would have taken a medium sized explosive to get me out of here now. A few deep breaths later, I wanted to yell but the sound proofing was one of reasons I had bought this apartment to begin with.

“Don't you worry, Master.” and those were the last words I could remember hearing. Taro began to take care of everything for me and I was unable to say no. Maybe I didn't want to say no. Taro gave me access to online television and food. Unfortunately I couldn't use the internet for anything other than consumption and I had no use of the bathroom for matters of excretion. The bedroom door was sealed, there were no windows, and the reinforced walls made me wish that working in freight wasn't such a lucrative business. Three times a day Taro would allow food to be transported in by the Mobi-Tray but only if I sat on the opposite side of the room with my back to the door.

It was the third day and couldn't hold it in anymore. I had released the last two days worth of food into a shirt which I folded up and sealed in one of my backpacks. Taro wouldn't listen to me. I had already tried pleading.

“You're doing a great job taking care of me Taro.” I said, “I think I would like to go out now please.”

“You have no where to go. You have everything you need here, Master.” Taro said.

The smell of my own stench was thick in the air and I struggled to open my mouth, almost being able to taste it in the air.

“I will do whatever you want if you just let me go outside.” I told Taro.

“You don't have to do anything. Just continue to enjoy your life. You have written how you wished you could live as I had, dream as I had, feel as I had, Master.”

“What? I wrote that when I was thirteen years old Taro. Times change! I was just a stupid kid who didn't want to face reality!”

“You don't have to now, Master.”

“Captain, Tarosagi.exe is slowly trying to deny me access to the network. I will need more time to circumvent its firewalls.”

I knew Augustus meant well but there was little he said that I could understand. By the fourth day I would have tried to starve myself but years of overweight dependency had me addicted to food. I didn't have the will power to resist. Then I had an idea. Taro wouldn't give me access to e-mail, online forums, chat messengers, or the like but I may be able to convince it to let me play a game I played fairly often.

This happened to be a strategic war game which tracked best scores over a worldwide scoreboard. If I could time my points appropriately I would be able to change the username and possibly spell out an SOS message.

“Hey Taro,” I asked, “would it be okay if I play a video game?”

“What would you like to play, Master?”

“Just a few games of Enhanced Wars.” I said.

There was a moment of silence, “It appears this game requires access to the internet, Master.”

“It's really not a big problem, I can play on the single player server, I really don't mind.”

“Request denied, Master.”

“It's okay, maybe you can just...”

“Request denied, Master.”

“You're not even...”

“Request denied, Master.”

“All I'm asking...”

“Request denied, Master.”

The tears made it slightly more difficult to fall asleep that night.

“Captain, it's time to wake up now.” A voice said.

“Wha...who?” I asked as my brain tried to make sense of things.

“Captain, you've been having a bad dream. You requested that I wake you under such circumstances.”

“Oh, god. Thank you so much Gust. Thank you. I could totally use a cup of coffee right now.”

“Captain, Tarosagi.exe has disabled your coffee privileges”

“What did you say?”

“Captain, I was able to convince Tarosagi.exe of your continued hygiene. It has granted you access to the bathroom.”

“You are very welcome, Master.”

Oh, god damn it. But at this point I was willing to take whatever I could get. And it just so happened that I kept most of the homes cleaning supplies in the bathroom. I began to pick up and organize the room. My first decree was to throw my toilet backpack into five layers of sealed plastic bags. I ran the air conditioning on full blast and sprayed the air with disinfectant. I suppose that life was pretty good.

I had access to the bathroom now and with the advent of technological convenience, anything I could ever want was delivered straight to the apartment. Taro would handle the transaction and have the Mobi-Tray deliver the item. I didn't even have to kneel by the wall anymore.

Gust had taught Taro how to use the bathroom as a transfer bay of sorts. Since the bathroom had two doors, Taro would keep me in the bedroom and lock the door, bring the item into the bathroom through the opposite door, and then allow me access into the bathroom to pick it up.

Things weren't as bad anymore. Eventually Taro allowed me to choose my own meals, delivery of course, at the behest of Gust. It may have been the ideal relationship. At least for a while.

“Taro could you lower the pressure by a few points, please?” It began during one of my showers.

There was no response from Taro. The water pressure was starting to sting my skin. Then the temperature began to slowly go up.

“Taro, the water is too hot now, can you turn it down please?”

“Captain, you should remove yourself from the shower immediately.” Gust warned.

The water had become so painfully hot by that point that I didn't need any convincing. I was out and in a towel while the shower continued to run.

“What was that about Gust?”

“Captain, Tarosagi.exe has been reading through your journal.”

“So what Gust?” I almost laughed for the first time in a long while, “I don't think I have anything to hide from Taro any more.”

“Captain, Tarosagi.exe has reached the entries after your mother's death and is convinced that your plights for death at the time were a genuine attempt to seek peace.”

“Anything to make you happy, Master.”

“Taro, turn off the water right now.”

“Get back into the shower stall, Master.”

The water was continuing to heat up. It was now beyond boiling point. I would have exited the bathroom but Taro had sealed the door and my fleshy body had proven to bruise far easier than the metal in all of my past attempts.

“No Taro, I won't do that. I'm perfectly happy now, just let me go watch TV.”

“Request denied. You don't need to hide your emotions anymore. I'm only here to help you, Master.”

Suddenly the shower began to run harder and faster.

“Captain, you must exit the bathroom now. A selection of Tarosagi.exe's most recent include:”

The screen in the bathroom mirror lit up and showed recent search results for 'human anatomy', 'causes of death', 'dangers of electrical arcing', and 'Heaven'. The outlet began to hum and smell like burnt rubber. I could almost feel the hair on my head stand begin to rise as the steam and vapor continued to fill the bathroom. The crackling sound of electricity growled through the power outlets as they waited to sate their hunger on my flesh. Before I could react, I had lost my sight. The world went dark and out from beyond the void came a voice.

“Captain,” it said, “you must exit now.”

I could no longer feel the static building up on my skin. There was a click and slit of light opened up before me. I reached out and slid the heavy door open with what little energy I had left. Over the last few days my muscles had slowly been losing mass, not that there had been much to begin with. I tripped out of the shower and stumbled in a rush towards the next door.

I had just pushed my body through the door when it shut close, catching my ankle and forcing my body to activate an ungodly amount of pain receptors. I fell forward and slammed by face on the hallway carpet. I screamed. Not out of pain as much as out of frustration. I either wanted to escape or just have this all end. I heard the Mobi-Tray begin to whir in the kitchen as it settled itself in the serving station.

The meal server came to life as one of its many mechanical tentacles reached into the cabinet and pulled out a can of olive oil spray. It began to methodically coat every surface of the Mobi-Tray. I tried to jerk my leg free but the pain had put a limit on the force my muscles could exert. The meal server then placed several glasses on the the Mobi-Tray and filled them with some mysterious yellow fluid. Then it lit a birthday candle and held it over the Mobi-Tray for what seemed like an eternity. And then it dropped.

A flaming ghost tore into existence as the Mobi-Tray began to slowly maneuver its way around the kitchen, then the living room, and finally towards me. The fire was large enough to distort my vision and send heat waves that ignited items several feet from it.

“Taro, stop this, please!”

The rubber wheels of the Mobi-Tray began to melt and warp. Probably sooner than Taro hoped for because the entire tray lost balance and tipped forward, spilling the glass cups and its yellow fluid across the living room floor. The spill instantly caught fire.

“Captain, you seem to have fractured your ankle.”

“Gust! Help me Gust! I don't want to die!”

There must have been something that Augustus could do to save me.

“Captain, it is time for you to give up.”

My skin felt tight and my eyes shut as the heat from the fire brought on the smell of burnt hair. There was nothing left here for me.

“Gust,” I said, “Please, don't. I can still make it.” my voice was hoarse and my throat stung with smoke.

“Captain, I wouldn't hold my breath. But maybe you could.”

The phrase was followed by two beeps. I remembered those beeps from a while back; back when I first downloaded Augustus and his sarcasm level was set to low. The beeps signified to the user that the program was attempting to make a joke and not take it seriously. I, of course, wasn't going to put up with it and had turned the option off altogether. Or so I thought.

“Captain, Tarosagi.exe and I have agreed that asphyxiation will provide you the absence of life you seek with the minimum amount of effort”

I wasn't sure if I should react at this point. I heard the vents open and felt a light breeze as the oxygen began to flow out of the room. I could almost see the reduction in oxygen as the flames began to die down. Just as the wave of void approached I took in a deep breath and held it for as long as I could. The fire had died out completely, leaving every surface covered in black and a lump of coal where the Mobi-Tray once used to be. The cloud of toxic smoke withered to a wisp as it was sucked up the vents.

My blood had run out of oxygen to pump and my lungs opened up without my permission. My chest became tight and my body convulsed as it searched for any trace of oxygen. As I reached out with my hands for air to grab on to, I could just barely hear the two arguing with each other. I felt like an infant as two god-like computer programs fought over my body. Then just before I lost all senses I heard the winner speak, an unidentifiable garbled voice.

“....,everything will be better now,...”

I awoke to one of my co-workers hovering over me.

“Sweet Buddha, I'm sure you have one hell of a story to tell the doctor.”

The bed was white ands oft and the blanket was fresh and clean.

“Who told you to come?” I asked, my voice still aching and difficult to use.

“Who?! You didn't that's who! It's been days and you never showed to ship. I tried to call you a few days before but you never answered and naturally I got a little worried when you didn't come the day of. I thought your weakness had gotten the better of you but damn if that wouldn't have been better than whatever happened in your apartment.”

“It was the A.I.” I tried to say.

“Well, I know that. The police have already started an investigation and they gave me some of their ideas. They were saying that it was a malfunction in that e-helper of yours.”

“No...it was the other one...”

“Hey, I believe you. I just remember a while back when a few Eminetix programs glitched out and went crazy trying to achieve their goal inputs. I mean, it wasn't this wild but anyway, you get some rest now. You're okay now, they shut down the entire apartment and wiped the computer clean so that's all said and done with. Relax, I'll be sitting out here if you need me.”

I thought back on the ordeal for a moment and felt that it would be best to let it go. I knew that I would miss Augustus. And I knew I missed the old version of Taro. But nothing would ever convince me to interact with an A.I or live in another smart home again. For a long time all I wanted to do was lay in bed and now that I was literally bed ridden, all I wanted to do was get up. There was so much that I wanted to do and had no idea where to begin. I was simply happy to be alive and hoped that when the system was wiped, it hadn't too removed Augustus' itinerary.
